factor_ratings.evidence: Owns a sub-block end to end; impact contained to defined component/workstream, felt across the team rather than the function

No indication of setting own approach on ambiguous problems; role description implies independent execution on a defined block, consistent with 'works independently on defined problems; outcomes reviewed, approach not'
Sub-block ownership implies defined problems requiring judgment among known RTL design approaches, not open-ended ambiguity requiring constructed solution paths
Title 'Senior Engineer' and sub-block scope indicate proficiency in RTL design discipline, delivering reliably without support, but no evidence of depth extending credibly into adjacent disciplines
Explicitly owns a sub-block end to end -- matches 5a anchor 'owns a block or module end to end'
No mention of influencing adjacent teams or partners; scope limited to peer-level influence through demonstrated work on the block

decision.governing_rule: rule 1: scope of impact is primary, and all factors here converge cleanly at L3
decision.alternative_reasoning: L4 requires ownership of a full subsystem across a development cycle and impact across the function, with ambiguous problems requiring constructed solution paths. The description specifies only a 'sub-block,' a narrower unit than a subsystem, and gives no evidence of cross-function impact, ambiguous problem framing, or influence beyond the immediate team, so L4 is not supported by the evidence provided.
decision.reasoning: All six IC factors point consistently to L3: the role owns a defined sub-block end to end (matching the L3 anchor for factor 5a exactly -- 'owns a block or module end to end'), with impact contained to the team, independent execution on defined problems, discipline-level proficiency without adjacent-domain breadth, and peer-level influence. No direct reports confirms IC track. Title 'Senior Engineer' is consistent with but not determinative of the L3 assignment -- the scope description (sub-block ownership, no cross-team or cross-function impact) is what drives the level per rule 6.
